groups.title: Republican Institutions
groups.context: Shared national institutions, available independently of party. Pompidou is President and Chaban-Delmas Prime Minister in January 1970. These focuses do not install a new head of state or a parallel election system.
groups.history: Fifth Republic; post-1968 social settlement; later alternation and decentralisation.

groups.title: Gaullists · UDR → RPR
groups.context: UDR/Pompidou governs at the start. Its New Society and presidential alternatives belong to exact subparty 1. The registered orthodox Gaullist current has a separate programme and completion ledger.
groups.history: Chaban’s New Society versus presidential primacy; participation versus national champions; social Gaullism versus later liberal turn.
groups.figures: Pompidou; Chaban-Delmas as Prime Minister; later Chirac

spirits.title: Presidential Republic
spirits.desc: A strong presidency and a disciplined parliamentary majority give the government considerable initiative. Central direction also sustains an extensive administrative apparatus.
spirits.resolve: The shared institutional branch changes the settlement; party turnover does not remove the Republic.

spirits.title: Unsettled Social Compromise
spirits.desc: The upheaval of 1968 has left a contested settlement between organised labour, employers and the state. Wage concessions and electoral victory restored order, but confidence in the social bargain remains fragile.
spirits.resolve: Social Settlement replaces this once with Social Mistrust (Stability -2%, no efficiency-growth penalty). A compatible social or electoral reform can remove the original or residual spirit, as shown in each focus; the two removals never stack.

spirits.title: Uneven Modernisation
spirits.desc: Large industrial programmes have transformed France, while regional access and local development remain uneven. The state’s capacity for major industry is real, and so is the gap between the capital and the provinces.
spirits.resolve: Regional Authority or Prefectoral State replaces this once with Modern Industrial Base: its existing +5% civilian-industry construction bonus is retained, and its -5% infrastructure-construction penalty is removed. That +5% is not a new focus grant.

unfinalised: Communist League / later LCR (slot 5): historically distinct revolutionary left; a national governing programme requires an explicitly alternate-history design, beyond PSU self-management.

Ordre nouveau (21), armed-forces government (22) and Orléans restoration (23): separate crisis/constitutional alternatives require their own reviewed accession and continuation. They are not silently represented by FN.
SAC (0), Enarchy (13), employers (15) and Proletarian Left (19): pressure groups or marginal revolutionary currents; no automatic full party tree solely because an MD slot exists.
No Islamic, Salafist or Shia governing branches are proposed for France. Existing religious/minority registry entries do not justify such branches.
Dedicated historically appropriate leaders beyond existing slots 1–3 must be authored and verified during a separately approved integration phase.

lifecycle.receipts: Native has_completed_focus checks against distinct party-specific focus IDs; separate one-time completion handling.
lifecycle.aggregation: Refresh clears only COLDWAR_FRA live programme totals, sums modifier deltas of completed focuses belonging to the exact current party identity, and attaches that one programme. It never replays completion effects or spirit replacements.
hooks: save/load initialisation using a supported existing project hook
lifecycle.legacy: In the 1970 scenario, the existing FRA_update_party_programmes hook must route to the Cold War refresh; leave the modern France handler for its own scenario.
lifecycle.cancellation: Native cancel_if_invalid=yes / continue_if_invalid=no with the exact party gate retained. No custom progress refund is proposed. An engine test must verify cancellation before implementation is considered complete.

rules: Exact governing subparty gates both focus availability and execution. Native cancellation flags handle a party leaving office during a focus; completion costs and grants occur only if the party guard remains valid. Engine cancellation/progress behaviour still requires testing.
Earned party modifiers deactivate on departure and reactivate on return. Only the current exact party/current may contribute; institutional reforms remain.
Related faction slots have separate focus IDs and earned ledgers. Changing from UDR to orthodox Gaullism or PCF to its old guard does not copy or block their focus receipts.

CID and FN have separate policy ledgers and focus IDs despite sharing registry slot 20. The existing dated identity change deactivates CID and enables FN; weekly identity refresh must cover this even when the numeric party index does not change.
One-time PP costs, stability effects and spirit replacements never repeat on government refresh, election, weekly tick or save reload.
Mutual exclusions are policy choices within each programme. A government change does not clear them. No free reshuffle or cross-party modifier stacking.
Cohabitation: MD has one governing-party variable. Proposed domestic authority follows that variable; a second independent presidency/prime-minister election model is not assumed.
Post-1968 and regional starting problems are replaced once by earned durable settlements; their party modifiers still follow the governing-party rule.
Recurring expenditure modifiers scale the existing weekly MD expenditure category. They are not fixed dollar payments or increases in the spending-law level.
This is the political sector only. Industrial, defence, nuclear, colonial and foreign-policy trees retain reserved neighbouring space until separately designed.

reference.approximation: Native source artwork and bitmap titles. External connector routing, state shading and camera simulation; not a running-game screenshot. Only the political sector is designed.
reference.effects_view: The same proposed focus columns and row order, with annotation spacing adapted to show numeric effects on every card. Native integer positions remain in the design data. This is a design view, not native in-game card dimensions.
reference.one_time_research: Native add_tech_bonus; 50%, uses=1; CAT_industry and CAT_construction have local 1968–1985 targets. Bonuses can be exhausted if all eligible technology is already researched.
reference.sector_layout: Each existing political/economic spine reserves its full footprint. Military columns +8/+12 and diplomatic columns +18/+22 connect to the existing substantive party entry at row 1. Adjacent governing programmes have a 30-column anchor stride. Filtered views include all real ancestors; they do not change native coordinates.
reference.offer_support: Individual modifiers, typed one-time effects, targeted event/decision patterns and timed ideas exist in MD. France-specific offer orchestration and party refresh are specifications awaiting implementation and engine verification.
reference.military_layout: Military columns +8/+12: existing force-structure choices at row 1; armament-industry choice at row 2; branch-specific delivery at row 3; exclusive research priority at row 4. OR joins permit either preceding programme; all native coordinates remain integer.

revision_summary.approval: Concept only. No loaded game files changed; implementation awaits explicit approval.

offers.title: Strategic and Industrial Consultations
offers.target: One sovereign country selected by the French player, other than France, with diplomatic contact and no war between the signatories.

lifecycle.proposal: The focus unlocks a targeted diplomatic proposal. The player chooses when to send it; the focus cost is paid once. Sending applies no agreement effects.
lifecycle.refusal: Refusal or 90 days without acceptance clears the pending offer. No agreement charge or benefit is applied.
lifecycle.acceptance: Recheck the completed focus, exact French governing party and dated identity, the current quoted recipient government, valid diplomatic contact, no war between signatories, current funds or Political Power, and eligible technology where applicable. Apply both sides together, once, or neither side.
lifecycle.government_change: Cancel pending proposals on either government change. End both temporary modifiers on either government change. A returning party requires fresh consent; it never replays setup charges or completed research/experience awards.
lifecycle.withdrawal: Either signatory may withdraw; immediately remove both temporary modifiers. Completed setup costs are not refunded. Existing one-use research awards are retained as acquired knowledge.
lifecycle.termination: War between the signatories, signatory removal, withdrawal or term expiry ends both temporary effects and clears references.
lifecycle.stacking: France may operate one accepted timed sector compact at a time across all party trees. The eight finite research exchanges can award their one-use research bonus once per completed offer focus; each bilateral pair may receive one French research-exchange award across all party changes. No repeated awards from reapplication, loading or party alternation.
lifecycle.renegotiation: Refused or expired proposals may be sent again. A consumed research offer cannot pay out again. A timed compact may be renewed only after expiry or withdrawal, with a fresh quote and fresh consent. Reapply any quoted immediate acceptance costs; recurring education-cost modifiers run only for the newly accepted term.

offers.weekly_cost_note: Cost modifiers add to the existing MD multipliers for the selected weekly expenditure base. They are not fixed dollar transfers and do not select a different spending law.

lifecycle.proposal: The focus unlocks a targeted diplomatic proposal. The player chooses when to send it; the focus cost is paid once. Sending applies no agreement effects.
lifecycle.refusal: Refusal or 90 days without acceptance clears the pending offer. No agreement charge or benefit is applied.
lifecycle.acceptance: Recheck the completed focus, exact French governing party and dated identity, the current quoted recipient government, valid diplomatic contact, no war between signatories, current funds or Political Power, and eligible technology where applicable. Apply both sides together, once, or neither side.
lifecycle.government_change: Cancel pending proposals on either government change. End both temporary modifiers on either government change. A returning party requires fresh consent; it never replays setup charges or completed research/experience awards.
lifecycle.withdrawal: Either signatory may withdraw; immediately remove both temporary modifiers. Completed setup costs are not refunded. Existing one-use research awards are retained as acquired knowledge.
lifecycle.termination: War between the signatories, signatory removal, withdrawal or term expiry ends both temporary effects and clears references.
lifecycle.stacking: France may operate one accepted timed sector compact at a time across all party trees. The eight finite research exchanges can award their one-use research bonus once per completed offer focus; each bilateral pair may receive one French research-exchange award across all party changes. No repeated awards from reapplication, loading or party alternation.
lifecycle.renegotiation: Refused or expired proposals may be sent again. A consumed research offer cannot pay out again. A timed compact may be renewed only after expiry or withdrawal, with a fresh quote and fresh consent. Reapply any quoted immediate acceptance costs; recurring education-cost modifiers run only for the newly accepted term.

offers.weekly_cost_note: Cost modifiers add to the existing MD multipliers for the selected weekly expenditure base. They are not fixed dollar transfers and do not select a different spending law.

military_research_contract.api: Native add_tech_bonus with one use and exact technology entries, never broad CAT_military/armor/aircraft/naval.
military_research_contract.scenario: Same-name local technology files override MD. Technology/project/DLC gates remain intact. Existing special projects are not completed or reactivated by these focuses.
military_research_contract.eligibility: Only the matching active DLC branch applies. Its required project must be completed and at least one quoted target unresearched. Mirror these guards at completion.
military_research_contract.ownership: The one-time research award and training experience remain earned national knowledge; neither is replayed by party changes or refresh. Industrial modifier deltas follow the exact governing party.
military_research_contract.exhausted: If all targets are already researched the research-only focus is unavailable. There is no invented future-technology or different-category fallback.
